hypotheses.claim: ActiveAssembly conflict-slot pressure should be explicitly observable before any conflict-allocation policy is changed.
hypotheses.prediction: On frozen H1 traces, conflict_slot_fraction and pressure_band will discriminate episodes in which ordinary high-value evidence is crowded out and will improve policy-comparison diagnosis without changing task semantics.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The telemetry adds no useful discrimination beyond existing selected packet IDs and re-expansion references.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched H1 trace analysis shows no additional predictive/diagnostic value after controlling for selected packet count, or the telemetry itself perturbs semantic identity/selection.

hypotheses.claim: No single fixed global conflict quota is likely to dominate across FRANK task regimes.
hypotheses.prediction: Matched live/reference tasks with different conflict density, correction cost and evidence asymmetry will produce a Pareto frontier between contradiction visibility and ordinary evidence retention.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One simple fixed quota dominates adaptive/grouped alternatives across outcome, correction, latency and context cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: A preregistered fixed quota wins or ties all primary metrics across frozen representative H1 traces and remains robust OOD.

hypotheses.claim: Conflict-group compression plus provenance-preserving selective re-expansion can reduce ActiveAssembly slot pressure without hiding actionable contradiction.
hypotheses.prediction: Grouped conflict representations achieve equal or better downstream correction and explicit contradiction recall using fewer local-4B slots than materializing every representative.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Grouping hides detail/provenance and increases false certainty or correction latency.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched traces show worse contradiction detection, provenance fidelity, correction time or outcome at equivalent context cost.

hypotheses.claim: A shared integrated Golden Trace identity across StateLedger, ActiveAssembly, WorkspaceEpisode and effect/outcome lineage will reveal mixed-epoch defects invisible in isolated component tests.
hypotheses.prediction: Fault injection around concurrent state updates, stale assemblies, receiver episodes and effect commit/re-entry exposes at least one cross-module inconsistency not caught by current isolated tests.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Existing per-component hashes/epochs already compose safely and an additional integrated trace contract adds only complexity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Exhaustive frozen fault corpus commutes across components with no mixed-epoch ambiguity and no additional diagnostic value from shared trace identity.

hypotheses.claim: Separating semantic_state_hash, state_version_hash and trace_root_hash is useful for H1/H2 replay and intervention equivalence.
hypotheses.prediction: The separation distinguishes semantically equal states reached by different histories and prevents false H1/H2 differential failures.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A simpler single-root ledger plus diagnostic metadata is sufficient and cheaper.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-host differential finds no downstream discriminator needing the separation or shows unacceptable recovery/cost complexity.

hypotheses.claim: Receiver-causal WorkspaceEpisode stages improve diagnosis/correction over an equally instrumented conventional EVENT_BUS null.
hypotheses.prediction: Matched lesions/corruptions are localized faster or corrected more reliably at comparable compute when addressability/delivery/reconstruction/uptake/causal-use/outcome/re-entry are separated.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The stage decomposition adds bookkeeping without task or diagnostic benefit.
hypotheses.falsifier: EVENT_BUS matches or beats verified outcome, diagnosis time, correction time and cost across preregistered traces.

hypotheses.claim: Typed recurrence control is useful only when estimator identity, uncertainty and freshness are explicit and when it beats fixed/event-driven baselines after overhead.
hypotheses.prediction: Typed control reduces false halts and stall burn on frozen trajectories at equal or better outcome-per-compute.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Fixed budget or ordinary event-driven scheduling is equally good or better after controller overhead/noise.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fixed/event-driven baselines match or beat typed control under matched trajectory and cost conditions.

hypotheses.claim: Constrained generation can improve structural admissibility of model/tool proposals but cannot substitute for deterministic semantic validation and external authority closure.
hypotheses.prediction: Grammar-constrained proposals reduce malformed outputs while fail-closed capability/effect checks remain necessary to block semantically invalid or unauthorized effects.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A simpler deterministic post-validator without constrained decoding achieves equivalent total correctness with lower latency/complexity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched tool traces show no incremental structural/selection benefit from constrained decoding or show degraded semantic tool choice that outweighs syntax gains.
